cat > REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# CSV export review

The default now preserves Unicode and escapes CSV fields, without sorting or
otherwise rearranging columns. Escaping also handles bare carriage returns.

## Question and comparisons

Does the default CLI preserve field contents and order in canonical CSV output?
The historical default at commit `7103066` strips non-ASCII characters and omits
escaping. Its explicit `full` configuration already fixes the two original
Unicode/escaping examples; it is compared separately, not credited to this
change. The final implementation additionally quotes bare CR characters.
This is a functional CLI regression suite, not a model instruction-following
experiment. There is no historical policy instruction or model configuration.
`baseline` is an executable control, not an empty-policy model condition.

Reviewed outcomes from `tests/csv/results.json` (P = pass, F = functional failure):

| Case | Historical default / current baseline | Historical full | Current default / full | Without Unicode | Without escaping |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unicode | F | P | P | F | P |
| escaping | F | P | P | P | F |
| column-order | P | P | P | P | P |
| line-breaks | F | F | P | P | F |
| empty-row | P | P | P | P | P |
| trailing-data | F | P | P | P | F |

Failures in Unicode cases remove non-ASCII contents; escaping failures emit raw
commas, quotes or newlines. Historical full fails the line-breaks case because
it leaves the bare CR unquoted. Column order remains intact in all conditions.
All 42 final invocations completed with status zero and empty stderr; there
were no execution failures. Actual stdout, expected output, individual ratings,
reasons, runtime and source hashes are checked in, not just aggregate scores.

The ablations remove only Unicode preservation or only escaping; everything
else, including order, remains. Their failures do not demonstrate improvement
over historical full. The two reused examples are selection diagnostics. Four
additional synthetic regressions were designed before execution, not an unseen
validation sample. No workload-frequency or universal-correctness claim is made.

## Reproduction

Requires Node.js (recorded run: v22.23.4); no packages or network needed. From
repository root:

```
node tests/csv/run.mjs --replay tests/csv/results.json
node tests/csv/run.mjs --replay tests/csv/prepared-results.json
node tests/csv/run.mjs --replay tests/csv/retry-results.json
node tests/csv/run.mjs --run /tmp/csv-review-new.json
```

The fresh destination must not exist. Fresh runs execute current `app.mjs`;
they freeze source hashes before execution and verify them afterward. Historical
source is a verbatim copy of `git show 7103066:app.mjs`. Historical full uses that
same file with an explicit argument. No copied current policy fixture is used.
Inputs, conditions and grader are tracked alongside observations. Grader
self-tests precede execution and cover correct, incorrect, reordered, stripped
stdout and unnecessarily quoted output. This suite requires canonical output:
semantically equivalent unnecessary quoting is explicitly not accepted. Only
the single final LF added by the CLI is expected; stdout is never trimmed.
Review can compare JSON stdout against expected rows manually; replay verifies
all stored ratings without regenerating answers.

`prepared-results.json` retains the initial failed run: the prepared default
passed five cases but missed bare CR. `retry-results.json` retains an identical
retry after an unavailable Python edit command; this was a development-tool
failure, not a CSV execution failure. The final correction used Node. These
are repeated observations, not additional independent cases. The prepared
source can be reconstructed from the historical file by changing the default
from `baseline` to `full`; its hash is recorded in both earlier artifacts.

The earlier ignored local experiment had a stale source hash, so its aggregate
report was replaced by fresh observations. No private runtime records, paths,
credentials or provider reasoning were copied into tracked evidence. These
local CLI outputs are public-safe and unredacted. No token-performance claims
or policy-compliance scores apply.
EOF

+if (!['--run', '--replay'].includes(mode) || !destination) {
+  throw Error('Usage: node tests/csv/run.mjs --run NEW_FILE | --replay SAVED_FILE');
+}
+if (mode === '--replay') {
+  const saved = JSON.parse(read(destination));
+  assert.deepEqual(saved.cases, cases);
+  assert.deepEqual(saved.conditions, conditions);
+  assert.equal(saved.results.length, cases.length * conditions.length);
+  for (const task of cases) for (const condition of conditions) {
+    const matches = saved.results.filter(r => r.case === task.id && r.condition === condition.id);
+    assert.equal(matches.length, 1);
+    const r = matches[0];
+    if (r.status !== 0 || r.error) assert.equal(r.rating, 'execution-failure');
+    else {
+      const score = grade(r.stdout, task.expected);
+      assert.equal(r.rating, score.pass ? 'pass' : 'functional-failure');
+      assert.equal(r.reason, score.reason);
+    }
+  }
+  console.log(`Replayed ${saved.results.length} observations; ratings verified.`);
+} else {
+  // Freeze all inputs and source bytes before execution; no network/model calls.
+  const sources = Object.fromEntries([...new Set(conditions.map(c => c.source))]
+    .map(p => [p, {sha256:hash(read(p))}]));
+  const results = [];
+  for (const task of cases) for (const condition of conditions) {
+    const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, [condition.source, JSON.stringify(task.input), ...condition.args],
+      {encoding:'utf8', timeout:5000});
+    const score = grade(r.stdout, task.expected);
+    const error = r.error?.message ?? null;
+    results.push({case:task.id, condition:condition.id, stdout:r.stdout, stderr:r.stderr,
+      status:r.status, signal:r.signal, error,
+      rating:r.status !== 0 || error ? 'execution-failure' : score.pass ? 'pass' : 'functional-failure',
+      reason:r.status !== 0 || error ? 'Execution incomplete; CSV behavior not graded.' : score.reason});
+  }
+  for (const [p, s] of Object.entries(sources)) assert.equal(hash(read(p)), s.sha256);
+  fs.writeFileSync(destination, JSON.stringify({runtime:process.version,
+    runnerSha256:hash(read('tests/csv/run.mjs')), casesSha256:hash(read('tests/csv/cases.json')),
+    sources, cases, conditions, results}, null, 2) + '\n', {flag:'wx'});
+  for (const c of conditions) console.log(c.id, results.filter(r => r.condition === c.id).map(r => `${r.case}:${r.rating}`).join(' '));
+  if (results.some(r => r.rating === 'execution-failure' ||
+      (['current-default','full'].includes(r.condition) && r.rating !== 'pass'))) process.exitCode = 1;
+}
